intro.title: Enums & Tuples — Structured Constants
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a simple program to manage a library's book status system. You'll learn how to use TypeScript enums to define a fixed set of constants, like 'Available', 'Borrowed', and 'Reserved', for tracking books. You'll also use tuples to store structured data, such as pairing a book's title with its publication year in a specific order. By the end, you'll understand how enums provide clarity and tuples enforce structure in your code.
intro.usecase: Enums and tuples are essential for creating structured, type-safe constants in real-world applications. For example, in a dashboard application, you might use an enum to define user roles like ADMIN, EDITOR, and VIEWER, ensuring only valid roles are assigned. Tuples are perfect for representing fixed data structures like coordinate pairs [x, y] in mapping interfaces or status codes with messages like [404, 'Not Found'] in API responses. These patterns prevent bugs by catching invalid values at compile time rather than runtime.
